content_voiceover: Here we return to the initiation phase diagram, now with factor five in the picture. The extrinsic tenase, tissue factor plus seven a, still activates factor nine and factor ten as before. But now the small amount of thrombin, factor two a, generated at the bottom has looped back with a white arrow to activate factor five into factor five a. That factor five a joins ten a and prothrombin on the membrane, forming the true prothrombinase complex, colored in and fully assembled. This is a key transition point, because a prothrombinase complex with factor five a on board is roughly a thousand times more efficient at generating thrombin than factor ten a acting alone. This feedback loop, thrombin activating its own cofactor, is the molecular switch that converts a trickle of thrombin into a self-amplifying cascade.
keypoints: Thrombin generated in initiation feeds back to activate factor five to five a
Factor five a joins ten a and prothrombin to form the full prothrombinase complex
Factor five a increases prothrombinase efficiency roughly a thousand fold
This positive feedback loop launches the transition into propagation
keypoint_voiceover: The big idea here is positive feedback: thrombin activates factor five, factor five a completes the prothrombinase complex, and thrombin generation jumps roughly a thousand fold. That feedback loop is the switch that turns initiation into propagation.
